translation: Target defines the following proposition: For every set K of closed first-order arithmetic sentences (in the language ℒₒᵣ), if every sentence in K is true in the standard model of the natural numbers ℕ, then either (1) there does not exist a recursively enumerable set of arithmetic sentences F whose set of classical first-order theorems (F.theory = {σ | F ⊢ σ}) is equal to K, or (2) there exists a closed arithmetic sentence σ such that σ is a Π₁ sentence (according to the syntactic hierarchy ℬ[<, ℒₒᵣ].Hierarchy 𝚷 1), σ is true in the standard model ℕ, σ is not an element of K, and the formal negation ∼σ is not an element of K. No further assumptions are imposed on K or F: K is not required to be deductively closed or to contain any base arithmetic axioms (such as 𝗜𝚺₁ or 𝗣𝗔), F is only required to be recursively enumerable (not Δ₁-presented or extending any base theory), the conclusion is written as a disjunction rather than an implication from the existence of F, and the incompleteness clause is stated in terms of set membership (σ ∉ K and (∼σ) ∉ K) rather than derivability from K.

divergences.description: In the source passage, K denotes a specific informal epistemic set (the propositions knowable or provable by the idealized human mind). Lean cannot express this epistemic notion directly, so Target instead universally quantifies over all sets K of true arithmetic sentences satisfying K ⊆ T.

Target restricts K, T, and F to sentences of first-order arithmetic (ℒₒᵣ) with truth in the standard model ℕ, whereas Gödel's quote speaks of mathematics in general and the quoted excerpt of Koellner does not explicitly fix the language of T and K (though the informal argument relies on arithmetic incompleteness).

Def6 formalizes 'there is a formal system F with F = K' as the existence of a recursively enumerable axiom set F in ℒₒᵣ whose classical first-order deductive closure F.theory equals K. Because Def6 appears negated in the disjunction, excluding non-classical formal systems or arbitrary r.e. machines not closed under classical first-order logic slightly weakens the statement for non-deductively-closed K.

Target requires the undecided true sentence σ to be syntactically Π₁ in ℒₒᵣ (ℬ[<, ℒₒᵣ].Hierarchy 𝚷 1 σ). This strengthens Koellner's Claim 3 (which imposes no complexity bound on φ), as the author explicitly intends, and idealizes Gödel's 'diophantine problems of the type specified' to the syntactic Π₁ hierarchy (equivalent to Diophantine unsolvability over ℕ via the MRDP theorem rather than literally a Diophantine equation).

judgement.summary: Target faithfully captures the logical structure and mathematical content of Gödel's disjunction as formulated in Koellner's Claim 3, with the soundness premise K ⊆ T made explicit and a Π₁ requirement added as claimed. The only divergences are minor idealizations inherent in formalizing the claim in first-order arithmetic: abstracting the epistemic set K via universal quantification, fixing the language and deductive closure to classical first-order arithmetic, and representing Diophantine problems via the syntactic Π₁ hierarchy.
